page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. At the head: the running title "LIBER." at left and the page number "589" at right. A fragment of italic text from the previous page opens the column, then one paragraph, then a centred heading in capitals with an italic subtitle, then one paragraph ending at the foot with the catchword "quam" at the right.

l.i: initium suscipiens à parte infima aqua, ut pro viribus

main_text.l: Hæc Picolominæus partim rationi consentanea,
partim repugnantia. Quòd enim illius fluxus, re-
fluxusque magis regimen Lunæ tribuat, id ratio-
nes prædictæ falsi evincunt, ut clarius ex dicendis
elucescet.
ARTICVLVS V.

l.i: Cur mare fit elatius in medio quàm juxta littus?

main_text.l: CAufæ æstus maris explicatio præmittit alius
causæ notitiam, Cur scilicet mare circa me-
dium magis, quàm juxta littus extollatur. Cujus
ratio facilis erit, si quæ verissima Picolominæus
mox docuit de halitibus, ac spiritibus calidis, quibus
mare gravidatur, memoriâ recolamus. Addamus
quæ in corpore animali docet Experientia, frigore
scilicet hyberno, partes calidiores intrò se recipere,
ac sese quasi in centrum cogere, ut propterea hyeme
animantia melius concoquant quàm æstate. Id au-
tem in aliis observare facile est, ex quo & terræ mo-
tus, & fulguris, & tonitrui, & complurium in aëre
inflammationum causa petenda est, ut suo loco ex-
plicabitur. Quantum verò præsenti quæstioni satis
est, consideremus flumina undique aquam frigidam
in mare advehere, quæ aqua circa littus[?] potissimùm
sese diffundat. Hinc Spiritus illi atque halitus, par-
tesque calidæ sese subducentes, haud secus atque
hyemali rigore calidæ animalis partes imum petunt,
undique in medium mare se contrahant: ubi propter
congregationem vim nactæ majorem rarefactione sui
mare inflent: quod tamen ibi consistat, facilè ad lit-
tus sese diffundat, ob amicitiam partium, quæ ut ma-
gis uniantur appetunt figuram globosam. Unde fit,
ut in scypho, vel alio vase aqua superemineat, ante-
quam

page.notes: The large initial C of the first word of the paragraph is joined to the word as "CAufæ"; the word is probably "Causæ" with the initial enlarged. "littus" in the paragraph near the middle is read with some doubt. Long s is written as plain s throughout (the printed ligature "ff" in "veriffima" and "fcilicet" is transcribed as "verissima" and "scilicet"). The word "quam" at the foot right is the catchword, and the paragraph continues on the next page. Small dark marks along the margins are stains and show-through, not printed text.
